title: An integral lift of an idempotent mod IB is a root of a monic polynomial congruent to x^d(x-1)^d
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $A\to B$ a ring map with $B$ integral over $A$. Let $b\in B$ be an element whose image in $B/IB$ is idempotent. Then there are an integer $d\ge1$ and a monic polynomial $f\in A[x]$ with $f(b)=0$ in $B$ and $f\equiv x^d(x-1)^d$ modulo $I$, i.e. the image of $f$ in $(A/I)[x]$ is $x^d(x-1)^d$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 09XG (lemma-helper-integral) and its proof (uses Algebra, Lemma Tag 00H5, lemma-integral-integral-over-ideal: an element of IB is a root of a monic polynomial with non-leading coefficients in I)

proof.text: *$z=b^2-b$ lies in $IB$.* The kernel of the quotient map $B\to B/IB$ is $IB$. The image $\bar b$ of $b$ is idempotent, so the image of $z=b^2-b$ is $\bar b^2-\bar b=0$, i.e. $z\in IB$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 09XG (lemma-helper-integral), first sentence ('Observe that z = b^2 - b is an element of IB')

proof.text: *An equation for $z$ over $I$.* Since $B$ is integral over $A$ and $z\in IB$, there is a monic $g=x^e+\sum_{j<e}a_jx^j\in A[x]$ with $a_j\in I$ for $j<e$ and $g(z)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-extended-ideal-element-monic]. If $e=0$, then $g=1$ and $1=g(z)=0$ in $B$, so $B=0$; in that case replace $g$ by $xg=x$, which is monic of degree $1$ with constant coefficient $0\in I$ and $(xg)(z)=0$. So we may take $g$ monic of degree $d\ge1$, $g=x^d+\sum_{j<d}a_jx^j$, $a_j\in I$, $g(z)=0$. (Stacks writes degree $d$ without the case $d=0$; this case is added by the agent.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 09XG (lemma-helper-integral), second sentence (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00H5, lemma-integral-integral-over-ideal)

proof.text: *The polynomial $f(x)=g(x^2-x)$.* Put $f=g\circ(x^2-x)=(x^2-x)^d+\sum_{j<d}a_j(x^2-x)^j\in A[x]$. (i) $f$ is monic of degree $2d$: $(x^2-x)^d$ is monic of degree $2d$ and each $a_j(x^2-x)^j$ with $j<d$ has degree $\le2j<2d$ (in Mathlib: Polynomial.Monic.comp, since $x^2-x$ is monic of degree $2\ne0$). (ii) $f(b)=g(b^2-b)=g(z)=0$, because evaluation at $b$ is a ring map and $f$ is the composite (Polynomial.aeval_comp). (iii) Reducing coefficients modulo $I$ is a ring map $A[x]\to(A/I)[x]$ commuting with composition (Polynomial.map_comp); it sends $a_j\in I$ to $0$, so $\bar f=(x^2-x)^d=x^d(x-1)^d$ in $(A/I)[x]$. Hence $d\ge1$ and $f$ are as required.

lean.statement: theorem exists_monic_aeval_eq_zero_map_eq_of_isIdempotentElem_quotient {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.IsIntegral A B] (I : Ideal A) (b : B) (hb : IsIdempotentElem (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A B)) b)) : ∃ (d : ℕ) (f : A[X]), 1 ≤ d ∧ f.Monic ∧ aeval b f = 0 ∧ f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = (X : (A ⧸ I)[X]) ^ d * (X - 1) ^ d
